## Patchset 2 on Gerrit 1980 — answering the `LLM-Review -1`

Took over the change from a prior session. Patchset 2 pushed; PS1's `LLM-Review -1` and
`Verified +1` were cleared by the upload, as expected.

### Finding 3 (`bugfix-size-attestation`) — already stale when it was reported, no restructuring

The reviewer blocked on "376 non-test lines, over the 150-line floor … verdict: unsigned; no
plan-review attestation record". Verified the line count independently against the Gerrit PS1
file list (9 + 25 + 301 + 17 + 24 = 376). The attestation claim was true at vote time and is
not true now:

| event | time (UTC) |
| --- | --- |
| review bot cast `LLM-Review -1` | 2026-08-21 07:27:53 |
| plan-review attestation `signed_at` | 2026-08-21 07:43:42 |

The attestation was signed **15m49s after** the vote. `rebar review-plan 8386-a512-4815-4e6b
--status` returns `{"ok": true, "verdict": "certified", "currency_basis": "file_impact"}` —
re-checked after all of the patchset-2 edits, from inside the worktree, and it did **not** flip
to `stale-code`. So the change was NOT decomposed to duck the line floor: a fix whose size is
legitimately authorised by a signed plan should not be carved up to satisfy a check that has
since been satisfied.

### Findings 1 and 2 — one cause: the declared janitor work was missing from PS1

Confirmed the parent diagnosis against the Gerrit file list. PS1 touched `cache.py`,
`delta_tree.py`, `repo_snapshot.py`, two docs and `tests/unit/test_repo_snapshot.py` — but
neither `src/rebar/_snapshot/janitor.py` nor `tests/unit/test_snapshot_janitor.py`, both of
which this ticket's own reviewed `file_impact` declares (`_evict credits bytes actually freed;
startup_sweep dedupes inodes` / `RED->GREEN oracle for shared-entry eviction accounting`). So
PS1 changed `entry_size` to charge `st_size // max(1, st_nlink)` and left every consumer of
that figure alone. This is `incomplete-implementation`, not a design error, and finishing it is
**inside** the authorised scope of the bug fix rather than a widening of it.

### What changed

The fix is to stop asking one function three different questions:

* `entry_size` — plain `st_size`. REPORTING only; it deliberately double-counts a shared blob.
  Reverted to its pre-change behaviour and kept as the subsystem's exported size primitive.
* `exclusive_size` — files with `st_nlink == 1`. The increment for **both** ends of the running
  total: populating adds exactly the bytes whose first link it created, evicting frees exactly
  the bytes whose last link it removes. Each inode is added once and subtracted once, so the
  incremental total tracks the authoritative walk with no drift and no rounding.
* `distinct_bytes` — each inode once. Ground truth for `startup_sweep`.

`_evict` now measures with `exclusive_size` before the rename-to-trash, so `free += reclaimed`
in the watermark loop credits bytes that actually left the disk; `startup_sweep` reconciles to
`distinct_bytes`; `materialize_tickets` and `cache.acquire` credit `exclusive_size` on populate.

The apportioned `st_size // st_nlink` is rejected and the ADR records why: it divides bytes
fairly for a report, but as an increment it credits a 1/k share of bytes still on disk, so the
free-space loop stops short of its watermark. Measured on the new fixture: evicting one of
three sharing entries credited **69,997 bytes while freeing 20,000**. Left uncorrected that
makes the original disk-exhaustion symptom worse, not better — the pass believes it recovered
space it did not.

Eviction policy, watermark semantics and the tunables are untouched.

### Both advisories closed

* `.ticket-write.lock` unshareable-inode contract
  (`test_write_lock_never_shares_an_inode_between_entries`): pinned **behaviourally** — a
  `flock` held through entry A must not block a non-blocking `flock` in entry B — plus the
  structural inode-distinctness assert, plus a guard that an ordinary unchanged blob IS shared,
  so the test cannot pass vacuously on a tree where the delta path never fired.
* `st_nlink > 1` accounting (`test_the_three_size_questions_on_a_known_inode_layout`): a
  hand-built layout with two links to one 1000-byte inode; every expectation is a literal read
  off the layout, nothing derived from the code under test.

### Non-tautological oracles + kill matrix

The janitor accounting tests measure the store with a per-inode walk written **separately** from
`cache.distinct_bytes` (documented as deliberate at the helper), so both sides of each assertion
can disagree — an accounting test that computes its expectation via the function under test
proves only that the code agrees with itself. Eight mutations, each on an independent side:

| # | mutation | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| M1 | `exclusive_size` -> `st_size // nlink` (the rejected apportionment) | KILLED |
| M2 | `exclusive_size` -> plain `st_size` (sharing ignored) | KILLED |
| M3 | `distinct_bytes` -> no inode dedupe | KILLED |
| M4 | `entry_size` -> `st_size // nlink` (the PS1 behaviour) | KILLED |
| M5 | `_evict` credits `entry_size` (pre-fix janitor) | KILLED |
| M6 | `startup_sweep` sums `entry_size` (pre-fix sweep) | KILLED |
| M7 | populate credits `entry_size` (pre-fix accounting) | KILLED |
| M8 | `delta_tree` drops `writes \| _unshareable(target_paths)` | KILLED (twice, independently) |

**M7 initially SURVIVED.** Every existing accounting test began with `startup_sweep`, whose
authoritative walk laundered any over-credit made at populate time — the two independent sides
were moving in step. Added
`test_populating_shared_entries_tracks_real_disk_without_a_sweep`, which never sweeps, and
which also asserts `sum(entry_size) > on_disk` so the equality it checks is discriminating
rather than satisfiable by any accounting. M7 then died. No survivors, no equivalent-mutant
claims.

M8 was checked twice: once whole (the structural inode assert fires), and once with the
structural assert disabled, to prove the `flock` leg kills on its own rather than riding along.

### Gates

`make lint` (incl. the shrink-only complexity ratchet: `active=49 new=0 increased=0 stale=0`),
`make typecheck` (614 files clean), full unit sweep **11944 passed, 44 skipped**. Largest
`src/rebar/_snapshot` module is 739 LOC, under the 800 cap.

Not closing the ticket: patchset 2 is awaiting `LLM-Review` and `Verified`.
